Subject: DPA question: notification timelines and evidence scope for hosted incidents

Hi Tessa,

Quick one as we're prepping our legal review: under Redwood's standard DPA, what are the realistic timelines and scope we can expect if Acme experiences a confirmed data incident involving PII for US patients? Specifically:

- Initial acknowledgement SLA (we typically have a 24h internal expectation)
- How quickly can Redwood provide logs, access records, and a forensic snapshot (not necessarily raw images) for hosted customers?
- Any limitations around subprocessor cooperation (e.g., if evidence lives with a third-party cloud provider)?
- Cross-border transfer constraints — can Redwood provide exports for our EU-subject data requests?

We're seeing differing language in the draft DPA redlines and need a concise playbook we can attach to our SOC/incident appendix.

If you have a short playbook or template you can share, that'd be really helpful — Procurement may want it attached to the purchase order.

Thanks,
Alicia

Hi Alicia —

Appreciate the heads up. I'm attaching a concise incident-notification playbook and a forensic handback template to use as a starting point (see attachments). High level summary below — happy to iterate with Legal/Procurement.

Proposed playbook (hosted API + Dedicated customers):
- Acknowledgement: within 2 hours of detection/confirmed report (business hours and automated ack outside hours).
- Preliminary findings: within 24 hours for incidents impacting availability/confidentiality where logs exist. This will include a summary of affected routes, model variants, and token-level telemetry available.
- Evidence package: up to 7 days for a full package (logs, KV-cache snapshots where applicable, request/response metadata). Large exports or full forensic images: by mutual action plan (MAP).
- EU/regulated subject data: we can prioritize exports; typical target is 48 hours for prioritized log exports (not raw disk images). Cross-border transfers will follow contractual transfer mechanisms (SCCs, approved safeguards) — we will not export encrypted customer secrets without customer authorization.
- Subprocessor cooperation: Redwood will coordinate required subprocessor engagement (cloud infra, telemetry vendors) and deliver their attestations where available. In rare cases where a subprocessor holds isolated evidence, we will broker the handoff and provide a summarized chain-of-custody.

Operational requirements we need from Acme to make this fast:
- Point-of-contact for forensics + procurement contact for any paid data egress work.
- Time window access: earliest timestamp and IDs for affected sessions or routes.
- Jurisdictional flags (EU subject data or HIPAA-sensitive).

Limitations/notes:
- For Private deployment (VPC or on-prem), we can provide tooling and runbooks; raw disk images from customer-controlled infra require a MAP and may be performed on-customer-site or via our approved third-party forensics vendor.
- Where KMS/HSM keys are customer-managed, we will not be able to decrypt protected payloads without an export key or a customer-signed request.

I've attached: redwood-dpa-incident-playbook.pdf (short playbook) and forensic-handback-template.docx. If you want, I can convert the playbook into a one-page appendix for your DPA and route it via DocuSign for signature.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-incident-playbook.pdf, forensic-handback-template.docx
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: Acme Health DPA — suggested concessions and operational caveats

Team — FYI, Acme asked for clarity. Draft response above (sent). A few items I want quick alignment on before we agree to any binding DPA appendix:

1) Timeline tradeoffs: I'm proposing 48h for prioritized EU log exports but keeping the full evidence package at 7 days. Legal asked if we can reduce full-package to 5 days for mid-size exports to be competitive. Thoughts?

2) Handback format: recommend we offer read-only forensic snapshots (S3 export + manifest + checksums) instead of raw disk images. This reduces our liability and avoids needing full disk-forensics workflows in hosted environments.

3) Subprocessor chain-of-custody: we should commit to brokering contact and sharing attestations, but not assume we can compel third-party vendors to produce data faster than their SLAs. We should surface that prominently in the appendix.

4) Commercial: if Acme wants expedited exports (under 48 hours for big datasets), propose an expedited egress fee and an SOW for forensic vendor time. We'll route pricing through Ben.

If everyone is good, I'll send the version with the 48h EU log export and the read-only snapshot language and include a DocuSign link for the DPA appendix.

Thanks,
Tessa

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the question and for looping Procurement. Based on internal alignment we've prepared a short DPA appendix and operational playbook that reflects what Redwood can commit to for hosted customers. Summary of the agreed items below and the appendix is attached:

- Acknowledgement: 2 hours (automated + human ack).
- Preliminary findings: 24 hours (summary of affected routes, telemetry snapshot).
- Prioritized log export (EU-flagged or HIPAA-in-scope): target 48 hours for read-only exports (CSV/JSON manifests, S3 export link with checksums).
- Full evidence package: target 7 days; for predictable mid-size exports we may be able to deliver in 5 days.
- Subprocessor cooperation: Redwood will coordinate engagement and provide available attestations. Where a subprocessor is the sole holder of evidentiary data, Redwood will broker the MAP and provide chain-of-custody documentation.
- Forensic handoff: we will provide read-only snapshots and metadata. Raw disk images and decrypted payloads require a MAP and customer authorization/keys.

DocuSign for DPA appendix: https://docusign.com/embedded/signing/abc123-addendum

3) If accepted, we'll route the appendix via DocuSign and add it as an exhibit to the SOW.
